title: Standing Seam on a Houston Home
description: Concealed clips, a PVDF finish, and a deck under the panels. That is a house roof, not an agricultural one.
html:
Standing seam is the metal roof people mean when they picture a clean house, not a shed. The seams stand up, the fasteners are hidden, and the panels can move when a Texas afternoon heats them and the night lets them go.

Clips, not screws through the face

Each panel locks to the next over a rib. Clips hold the panel to the deck and still let it expand. That is the point. Screws driven through the flat of the panel pin it in place, and the hole becomes the leak when the washer dries out. If a bid is “metal” and the fasteners show in the field of the panel, it is a different system. Ask which one you are buying.

Under the panels there should be a solid deck and underlayment. That is what keeps rain noise ordinary and gives the roof something to fasten to if a branch lands. Oil canning, a slight waviness in the flat of the panel, is a look, not a leak. Good installers limit it. They do not promise a mirror.

Finish and hail

A PVDF finish, the family people call Kynar, holds color in this sun better than a cheap polyester coat. Hail can still dent the panel. Dents that do not open a seam are often called cosmetic on a policy. Read that exclusion before you choose metal for hail country and expect every dimple to be replaced.

Details that leak on metal

The panels are the easy part. Leaks show up at the ridge, the eave, a pipe, and any place a panel was cut and depended on sealant instead of a hem. We flash those the way the system is drawn, not with a bead of caulk as the only defense. If your roof is a simple gable, metal is straightforward. If it is full of dormers, the detail work is the bid, and it should look like it.

HOAs in the suburbs sometimes allow standing seam and ban everything else metal. We check before we draw it. If your house is a candidate, we will price metal roofs against asphalt shingles on the same inspection. Request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
